header: DOES THE RESULT HAVE ROOM WITH THE BUTTON PANEL ON TOP OF IT? (my rule, 27 Nov 2026, from the owner's own idea) The two rows of choices under the search box (Search in, More tools) take two or three lines of the window. Taking them away for EVERY result was too much: a small answer (a calculator's, a one-line reply) fits with the panel and no scroll bar, and there the choices are useful. So the panel leaves only when the result would NEED A SCROLL BAR with it there. room = the most the window may be tall (its max-height) - everything in it except the scroll area (the box, the panel, any notice) the panel keeps its place when the result's own height (scrollHeight of the scroll area) is no more than `room`. (The box above it also shrinks to the lines of the question when the panel has gone: inputRows.ts. The room is measured as if the box had its default height, so that the two do not chase each other.) The result's height does not depend on whether the panel is shown, so the decision cannot chase itself (panel goes -> result looks shorter -> panel returns -> ...). To keep the panel from flickering as a result changes a little (a card that grows as you type, a list that loads), it takes a margin of HYSTERESIS to change its mind: it leaves when the result is taller than the room, and returns only when the result is shorter than the room by HYSTERESIS pixels. It is measured before the screen is painted, so the panel never shows for a frame and then goes.

symbols.name: HYSTERESIS
doc: The margin, in pixels, a result must be below the room before a panel that left may return.

symbols.name: panelKeepsPlace
symbols.sig: export function panelKeepsPlace(contentHeight: number, roomWithPanel: number, shownNow: boolean, hysteresis = HYSTERESIS): boolean
doc: The decision, as a plain function (so it can be tested): given the result's height, the room it has WITH the panel, and whether the panel is shown now, does the panel keep (or get back) its place? `roomWithPanel` is what the scroll area could be if the panel were there.

params.name: { active, modalRef, scrollRef, panelRef, inputRef, defaultRows }
params.type: { active: boolean; modalRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; scrollRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; panelRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; inputRef?: RefObject<HTMLTextAreaElement | null>; defaultRows?: number }

doc: Returns true while the panel may stay, false when the result needs the room. `active` says that a result is on the screen at all (when it is not, the panel stays). The three refs are the window (with the max-height), its scroll area, and the panel (which is not drawn while it is away: I remember its last height).

behaviours: a result that fits with the panel (no scroll bar) keeps it; one that would need a scroll bar sends it away
a panel that left comes back only when the result is shorter than the room by the margin: no flicker around the line
the same result, in a window the same height, gives the same answer whether the panel is shown or not once it is clear of the margin (the decision cannot chase itself)

it is measured before the paint (a layout effect), with a resize observer for what changes by itself, from the window's max-height and everything in the window but the scroll area, remembering the panel's height while it is away
the omnibar uses it: the panel's wrapper, the scroll area's ref, and the deep answer always takes the panel away
